picks.title: Impossible Objects superpowers VFX production with AI models running on HP ZGX Nano
picks.excerpt: LA studio Impossible Objects is running AI models locally on HP ZGX Nano desktops so artists can fold generative steps into an existing VFX pipeline without shipping plates to the cloud. The piece details how artist-driven AI workflows sit alongside traditional comp and 3D tools.
picks.rationale: The most actionable item in the pool — a working studio shows how to keep plates on-prem and still put generative steps inside a normal comp and 3D pipeline.

picks.title: Nura Studios Debuts 'Rainbow Hollow' Stop-Motion Styled AI Series
picks.excerpt: Noah Wagner's new series was produced on Nura's Showcraft platform, which handles story, layout, animation, edit and post finishing inside one environment. The system opens to the public in early September.
picks.rationale: A single-environment production platform with a dated public opening — a finished series is the proof, and early September is the date to plan around.

picks.title: Vida Scene Search: AI Scene-Level Search, No Manual Logging Required
picks.excerpt: Vida added an offline AI indexing layer to its Content OS MAM so post teams can search inside video libraries at the moment level. It removes the dependency on metadata that was hand-logged years ago.
picks.rationale: Moment-level search over an unlogged archive changes a concrete daily chore for post and archive teams, and the indexing runs offline.

picks.title: A New Free Seminar Teaches Documentary Filmmakers When and How to Opt Out of AI
picks.excerpt: Field of Vision and Freedom of the Press Foundation are running the sixth edition of their Digital Security Clinic, this time on AI. It walks documentary teams through where AI enters their pipeline and how to opt out of it.
picks.rationale: The rare opt-out playbook: a free, dated clinic that maps where AI quietly enters a doc pipeline and how to switch each entry point off.

picks.title: Peacock Launches First Serialized Mobile Game 'Public Eye'
picks.excerpt: Peacock's first episodic interactive title comes out of NBCUniversal's pact with Wolf Games, the generative-AI startup co-founded by Elliot Wolf. It is a test of AI-generated serialized storytelling built by a TV production house.
picks.rationale: A major streamer shipping an episodic generative-AI title is a new delivery format, not another pilot deck — the first real read on whether it holds an audience.
